subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: After the registration-mode bug is fixed, should OpenClaw accept `@microsoft/mxc-sdk@0.7.0`/`node-pty`, packaged MXC executor binaries, argv-carried base64 config, and fail-closed protected-skill `rw` behavior for this official external Windows sandbox plugin?
rationale: Automation can add the missing registration guard, but accepting native sandbox dependencies and the preview SDK config transport is a maintainer/security boundary decision.

options.title: Fix Scope Then Approve Exact Head
options.body: Add the `api.registrationMode !== "full"` guard and focused test, then have maintainer/secops approve the exact dependency graph and documented preview-SDK boundary before merge.

options.title: Require Stronger Runtime Boundary
options.body: Pause the PR until MXC provides a non-argv config transport or OpenClaw implements a maintainer-approved alternative and working read-only overlay behavior.

options.title: Defer First-Party MXC
options.body: Keep the implementation out of the official OpenClaw release path until the native dependency and sandbox semantics are mature enough for support.

recommendation.title: Fix Scope Then Approve Exact Head
recommendation.body: Add the `api.registrationMode !== "full"` guard and focused test, then have maintainer/secops approve the exact dependency graph and documented preview-SDK boundary before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` is the live assignee and the remaining acceptance call is a maintainer/security boundary decision.
